Changelog

datagoodr (development version)

New

The DGF carries a two-axis guess and a suggested stabilizer (formex v7)

formex v7 models a value’s format as (semantic_type, format_style, unit_type) and exposes stabilization as a transform-path search. datagoodr now records and acts on that:

  • guess_* columns capture formex’s route leaf as two axes — guess_format_style (the written rendering) and guess_unit_type (the dimensional/categorical unit) — alongside a human guess_label (calendar {{ date :: temporal }}), guess_match_kind (the honesty column), and guess_variant_id/guess_depth/guess_confidence.
  • desired_* gains the matching target form (desired_semantic_type, desired_format_style, desired_unit_type), and create_dgf() fills a suggested stabilizer — a read :: [convert] :: write plan from formex::fx_plan_transform() — previewing its effect in stable_first5. A reformat the registry cannot reach is reported not-transformable, never guessed.
  • stabilize_data(use_v7 = TRUE) executes those plans with formex::fx_apply_plan() — vectorised and type-preserving. It is opt-in: the default is unchanged, and a legacy raw_to_stable_transform / desired_data_import_rule, where set, always takes precedence.

The flip is additive: desired_data_type/desired_data_class remain the render engine’s dispatch contract.

create_dgf() reads both of formex’s predictions

formex returns two answers per column — the v6 $route (a four-level ontology path that truncates gracefully) and the legacy $guess (a detector at a pass rate). They are complementary, so datagoodr now reads both:

  • The route wins when it resolves to a confident leaf. It reaches types no detector emits — a bare four-digit year is temporal/period/year to the router and nothing at all to the detectors, so year columns are now typed temporal instead of falling through to text.
  • The legacy guess wins where the route truncates, which is every zero-padded numeric key (FIPS, ZIP, EIN) and email address.

desired_data_class now carries v6 coordinates directly. No translation was needed: the v4 dotted vocabulary turned out to be a subset of v6’s semantic_family.semantic_type, so the column already spoke v6.

Two guards keep a wrong prediction from corrupting a column:

  • The storage-safety gate. A number/* route may not re-type a column that .safe_numeric() refuses to promote. The same rule that stops read_as_text = TRUE turning 06037 into 6037 now stops the router doing it. One predicate, both directions.
  • Confidence is not sufficient. A column of rnorm() doubles routes to text/web/domain at depth 4 with confidence 1.0, because -0.6264538 parses as a domain name. So the route may refine a coarse text base type or supply a strong semantic signal, but it may not overturn a type read from storage.

When neither modality is confident the column keeps its base type, and the route’s depth is recorded rather than discarded — a truncated path is a valid partial answer for a reviewer to deepen, not a failure.

Breaking changes

Type detection moved to the formex package

datagoodr no longer contains the data-type detection library. It now lives in formex, which datagoodr imports.

The two packages split along a clean line: formex is the engine (one column at a time, stateless — the type ontology, the detectors, guess_data_type(), fx_stabilize()), and datagoodr is the workflow (a whole data frame, human-in-the-loop — profiling, the Data Governance File, review and override, applying stabilization, writing outputs).

104 functions were removed from datagoodr’s namespace, including all 80 is_* detectors, guess_data_type(), score_data_type(), and the AutoType test-case helpers. Code that called them needs one of:

library(formex)          # attach it, and existing calls keep working
formex::is_ein(x)        # or qualify each call

is_factor() and is_factor_df() are not affected — those are datagoodr’s own cardinality helpers, not detectors, and remain exported.

Also moved to formex: the data_type_tests dataset, the data-types/ ontology tree, the internal geography/code lookups in sysdata.rda, and the four detection vignettes (Data-Type Detectors, The Data-Type Ontology, Guessing a Data Type, Formex). Their current versions are on formex’s documentation site.

Install formex with:

remotes::install_github("lecy/formex")

Rule functions renamed: as_* -> read_*

A rule that ingests a written format now says so in its name. as_mmddyyyy() never produced mm/dd/yyyy — it consumed it and returned a Date. The name said the opposite of the function.

The convention is now:

  • read_<format>() ingests a value written in that format. The name states the input. These belong in raw_to_stable_transform.
  • as_<type>() coerces a value into a target type. The name states the output. These belong in desired_data_import_rule.

This makes the DGF’s two bridge columns distinguishable on sight — a rule sitting in the wrong column is now visible without running it.

old new
as_date(x, format) read_date(x, format)
as_datetime(x, format) read_datetime(x, format)
as_yyyymmdd() read_yyyymmdd()
as_mmddyyyy() read_mmddyyyy()
as_ddmmyyyy() read_ddmmyyyy()
as_mdyyyy() read_mdyyyy()
as_dMyyyy() read_dMyyyy()
as_Mdyyyy() read_Mdyyyy()
as_yyyymmddHHiiss() read_yyyymmddHHiiss()
as_mmddyyyyhhiiA() read_mmddyyyyhhiiA()
as_yyyymm() read_yyyymm()
as_yyyy() read_yyyy()
as_mm() read_mm()
as_EIN() read_ein()
as_id() as_id() (unchanged — it names a type)

The old names still work as deprecated shims that warn once per session, so a DGF whose rule cells carry them keeps running. They will be removed in the next minor version. Update rule cells in your DGF .xlsx/.csv files.

read_ein() returns the canonical hyphenated form

as_EIN("12345678") returned "012345678"; read_ein("12345678") returns "01-2345678". This matches the stable form the type ontology declares for identifier / id / administrative (ein), so a datagoodr-stabilized EIN and a formex-stabilized EIN are now the same string.

Bug fixes

  • A compact date label now reads the run-together form. as_yyyymmdd("20190315") returned NA — the exact case the compact label exists for. A label names the element order, not the punctuation, so read_date() now compiles both a delimited and a run-together pattern and picks per value. read_yyyymmdd("20190315") and read_yyyymmdd("2019-03-15") both parse.

  • read_yyyy() accepts a fiscal-year prefix. read_yyyy("FY2019") returns "2019".

  • read_yyyymm() validates its input rather than silently slicing any string, and accepts an already-hyphenated value.

Internal

  • .safe_numeric() — the rule deciding which character columns create_dgf(read_as_text = TRUE) may promote to numeric, and therefore what keeps 06037 from becoming 6037 — moved from the (now formex-owned) detector helpers into datagoodr’s own utilities, where it belongs.

  • R/01-06-guess-dgf-types.R is now the documented formex seam. It reads only formex’s public return value and touches no internals.
